newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Receiver named to Singapore election libel case.
newsitem.headline: Receiver named to Singapore election libel case.

text.p: A Singapore court has appointed a receiver to investigate the assets of an opposition politician being sued for libel by the country's leadership, a lawyer said on Tuesday.

The lawyer, who is close to the cases against Tang Liang Hong resulting from January's general election campaign, said the High Court appointed the receiver on Monday and told him to report back in two weeks.
"The receiver will begin his investigation and must report to the court within 14 days with recommendations for action," the lawyer, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong and Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew had asked for a receiver to be appointed.
The Straits Times newspaper said Goh and Lee had argued that Tang might dispose of the assets to avoid paying up if he lost the libel cases.

A court has ordered Tang, who ran for the Workers' Party in the elections and lost, and his wife, Teo Siew Har, to set aside up to Singapore $11.2 million (US$7.9 million) for possible damages in the suits.
In the campaign Goh called Tang a "Chinese chauvinist" dangerous to Singapore's racial harmony. Tang called Goh and other ministers who supported him liars.
Tang left Singapore soon afterwards, saying he had received death threats. He is now in London consulting lawyers on his defence and has stopped talking to reporters.
Legal sources said that if Tang and his wife failed to cooperate with the receiver, he could be found in contempt of court. It could also lead to seizure of their assets.
Lawyers acting for the Tangs were not available for comment.
